prize_parts.citation: For a visionary, densely patterned body of Romanian prose, rooted in poetry, that builds memory, the body and dream into an expansive metaphysical architecture.

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged from round 1: Cărtărescu, with a narrower citation. On the common criteria, the voice is recognizable within a page. It is long, rhythmically driven, hallucinatory prose in which the body, memory, Bucharest and metaphysical speculation form one construction. The formal achievement is structural as well as stylistic. As far as public knowledge shows, the Blinding (Orbitor) trilogy and Solenoid are built as large architectures, not as accumulations of episodes. The oeuvre spans several decades, and the poetry that precedes the prose gives it a lyric root. I take the case to concern the whole body of work, which fits the principle that a whole authorship is judged and not a single book. I have revised the citation. In round 1 I credited prose and poetry as a real second strand. Several colleagues, and my own uncertainty, show that the poetry and early work cannot be assessed on the translated evidence. The citation therefore rests on the prose and names poetry only as its root. I did not move on the ranking because the open reservations (repetition, translation) have not been answered by any new evidence in the exchange. They have only been restated by all sides. The shared first-choice or alternative status of B045 and B004 among colleagues is not evidence of literary merit, and I do not use it that way.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is unresolved. Olsson and others suspect that the very long late novels recycle bodily and dream imagery instead of developing, and I cannot rule that out. If a reader of the Romanian originals found the late volumes mostly reworking earlier material, the claim to sustained development would weaken a great deal, and Carson's economy would look stronger by comparison. Second, the prose depends on rhythm and syntactic density, which I can judge only through translation of uncertain quality. Third, a visionary, inward and encyclopedic method may invite large interpretive readings. The case must show the effect in the sentences and the construction of the books, not in a critic's metaphysical gloss. I raised the same caution about Can Xue's work being read as allegory, and I apply it to my own first choice.

responses.point: Olsson keeps Can Xue first. He accepts the dilemma of consistency versus depth and says the open point is whether her later books alter the terms of her method. He proposes anonymous regional expert reports on her Chinese prose. He also weighs the length and recurrence of Cărtărescu's novels more heavily than Mattson does.
responses.response: I agree that an expert report is the right procedural answer for Can Xue, and that translation limits are not a reason to rank her lower in principle. That is why she remains one of my alternatives. For now the difference between us is evidential. For Cărtărescu, colleagues who have read the late cycle say it extends the earlier project, and I have no verification to the contrary. For Can Xue, her defining feature is a stable method, and the question of development is open even among her supporters. If a report showed that her later books change scale, form or relation to the short fiction, I would move her up. Your recurrence point against Cărtărescu has the same standing. I keep it as my main risk and cannot dismiss it from this record.

responses.point: Carlberg ranks Carson first by a narrower margin than at opening. She suggests building a Carson citation on original poetry, essay and hybrid narrative, with translations as context only. She also argues that a compact, formally varied corpus can show sustained quality and that scale is not depth.
responses.response: I accept that scale is not depth, and I do not rest my choice on length. My preference for Cărtărescu is based on evidence of continuity of project, which I find easier to see in a single constructed world than in a varied corpus. Your citation wording does reduce my scope worry about the translations, and it makes the Carson case more coherent than it looked in my round-1 answer to Mattson. On that basis I now name B004 as my first alternative. I still have two doubts that your reply does not close. I cannot tell how much of Nox's force depends on its form as an object. I also cannot tell which works beyond Autobiography of Red and Nox carry the claim of a durable core. You have told us you cannot verify the later volumes either.

responses.point: Palm holds Carson first. She argues that the durable core is the original work (verse novel, lyric and essay hybrids, the elegy in Nox) and that line-level control and formal economy outweigh scale. She grants that Cărtărescu's architecture is real. She names the length and recurring motifs of the late novels as her hesitation.
responses.response: Your point about line-level control is the strongest version of the Carson case, and I have taken it seriously. Where we differ is how to weigh formal economy against sustained construction. I do not think the criteria settle that alone, since they list both formal achievement and sustained quality. For me the deciding consideration is that the Cărtărescu case is a case of a single project continuing over decades, while the Carson case depends on a central core that supporters and doubters both say they cannot confirm beyond two or three books. We share the hesitation about repetition in the late novels. If the committee's readers of Romanian were to find that the repetition is a matter of method and not variation, that would favor your position, and I would say so.

responses.point: Mattson ranks Cărtărescu first and asks that the citation stay with the prose, with poetry as the stated root, until the committee has more evidence on the poetry. She also says the case must show the effect in the construction of sentences and books, not in the critic's reading.
responses.response: I agree on both points, and my revised citation follows your formulation: prose at the center, poetry named only as a root. This changes my round-1 wording, which gave the poetry a larger role than the evidence in this record supports. I also take your point that comparison of several translations, or readers of the original, should come before any final judgment of the sentences. I would add that the same standard should apply to every shortlisted candidate, since the translation limit does not favor one of them over another.

responses.point: Sem-Sandberg ranks Cărtărescu first and distinguishes repetition of motif from repetition of method. He says the recurring images are structural to a project that develops. He places Carson second and Can Xue fifth, with translation as the limit. He rests his preference on development and scale.
responses.response: The distinction between repetition of motif and of method is useful, and I would adopt it as the test for the late novels. The test needs evidence that neither of us can supply from translation: does a recurring image change function from one volume to the next? On that evidence I currently side with you, but I treat it as provisional. I would not rank Can Xue as low as you do for the reason you give. Translation limits our evidence for her and for Cărtărescu alike, so it cannot separate them. The reason to put her below him is the unsettled development question, not translation. I also agree that the post-communist context should not carry any part of the literary case.

uncertainties: I have not read the Romanian originals and have not independently verified any source. My judgment of Cărtărescu's prose rests on general public knowledge and on translations of uncertain quality.
Whether the late long novels vary and develop the project or recycle imagery is unresolved. No member has evidence beyond general public knowledge, and it is the main risk to my configuration.
The poetry, early prose and essays are unevenly covered in translation, so the citation is limited to the prose with poetry as root. Even that wording rests on less direct evidence for the poetry.

For Can Xue, whether the method develops across a very large output and whether her sentence-level strangeness survives translation are unresolved. My ranking of her is provisional and could change with a competent regional expert report.
For Carson, which works besides Autobiography of Red and Nox form a durable core, and how much of the effect depends on book design and classical apparatus, remain open.
Carlberg is a co-opted member whose voting status is undocumented, so any count involving her vote is a modeling assumption and not evidence of merit.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. The profile documents shared committee and 2019 election-round connections with colleagues, plus Swedish Institute, Arts Council and Nordic Council programme engagement, but no documented connection to any shortlisted writer. Her public remarks about women's authorships and her own novelistic practice are context only and not evidence of preference for any candidate. This is disclosed and not adjudicated.
